x: This item is doubtful: Andhra State, India's first linguistic state, was actually formed on 1 October 1953, not in April. April 1953 is keyed because it is the only 1953 option; November 1956 is when Andhra Pradesh was formed.
t: Discriminate Andhra State (1953) from Andhra Pradesh (1956).

x: This item is doubtful: all four statements are true. Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State, Gopala Reddy its last CM, Sanjiva Reddy the first CM of Andhra Pradesh, and C.M. Trivedi the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh (1 November 1956). Option B is keyed only by default.
t: Check each office-holder against the state and year.

x: Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State, Neelam Sanjiva Reddy the first CM of Andhra Pradesh, Chandulal Madhavlal Trivedi the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh and Nallapati Venkatramaiah the first Speaker of Andhra State, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the first holder of each office.

x: All four are correct: Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitram was the first Telugu novel, Satya Doota (Bellary) the first Telugu journal, Andhra Prakasika the first political journal, and the Bible the first book printed in Telugu.
t: Check each Telugu literary first separately.

x: Both are true: the first Andhra Mahasabha met at Bapatla on 26 May 1913, and Govinda Rao Nanal was the first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The first widow remarriage in Andhra was in 1881, P. Anandacharyulu became the first Telugu INC President in 1891, the AP Legislature became bicameral in 1958 and the first World Telugu Conference met in 1975, giving A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the events by year.

x: All four are taken as correct: the Satavahanas were the first historical Deccan dynasty, Harihara-I founded Vijayanagara, Devaraya-I is credited with first enlisting Muslims in the army, and Warangal faced its first Muslim invasion in 1303. Note that many texts credit Devaraya-II with large-scale Muslim recruitment.
t: Check each historical first separately.

x: The Dutch set up their first Andhra factory at Masulipatnam, the English at Machilipatnam in 1611, Ryotwari was first tried in the Baramahals, and Hyderabad was the first state to sign the Subsidiary Alliance (1798), giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Use the 1611 date to separate the English factory from the Dutch one.

x: Nallapati Venkatramaiah was the first Speaker of Andhra State, Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao the first Speaker of the AP Assembly, N. Sanjeeva Reddy the first Deputy CM of Andhra State and K.V. Rangareddy the first Deputy CM of Andhra Pradesh, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Discriminate Andhra State offices from Andhra Pradesh offices.

x: Both are true: Bezawada Gopala Reddy was the last Chief Minister of Andhra State (1955–56), and the AP Legislature became bicameral when the Legislative Council was created in 1958.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Nyapati Subba Rao was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle, Govinda Rao Nanal of the Hyderabad State Congress, M. Annapurnayya the first Secretary of the Socialist Party's Andhra unit and N.G. Ranga the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the first leader of each organisation.

x: P. Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress, presiding over the 1891 Nagpur session. Nyapati Subba Rao and Govinda Rao Nanal are linked with Andhra and Hyderabad bodies, not the INC presidency.
t: Recall the 1891 Nagpur session President.

x: Mulla Abdul Qayyum was the first Muslim leader from Hyderabad to join the Indian National Congress. B. Ramakrishna Rao was Hyderabad's first elected Chief Minister, and Anandacharyulu was the first Telugu INC President.
t: Recall Hyderabad's early Congress pioneers.

x: B. Ramakrishna Rao became the first elected Chief Minister of Hyderabad State in 1952. Prakasam and Gopala Reddy headed Andhra State, and Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh.
t: Discriminate Hyderabad State from Andhra State leaders.

x: The Kakinada Riot Case (1907) was the first criminal case of the Vandemataram Movement in Andhra. Chintapalli is linked with Alluri Sitarama Raju and Palnadu with the Forest Satyagraha.
t: Link each place to its movement.

x: Alluri Sitarama Raju began the Rampa revolt of 1922 by attacking the Chintapalli police station first. Palnadu is linked with the Forest Satyagraha and Kakinada with the Vandemataram riot case.
t: Recall the first target of the Rampa revolt.

x: The Forest Satyagraha during the Non-Cooperation Movement first started in Palnadu in Guntur district. Chintapalli belongs to Alluri's revolt and Bapatla to the first Andhra Mahasabha.
t: Link each place to its movement.

x: The first Kisan School was at Nidubrolu, the first World Telugu Conference met in 1975, Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the first Telugu Jnanpith and H.M. Reddy was the first Telugu cinema director, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall each Telugu first.

x: Harihara-I was the first Vijayanagara ruler, Devaraya-I is credited with first enlisting Muslims in the army, Kulottunga-I was the first Chalukya-Chola emperor and Nannaya began the Telugu Mahabharata, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the first of each kind.

x: Vijayawada (Bezawada) hosted the All-India Congress Committee meeting of 1921, the first all-India Congress gathering in Andhra. The first full annual session in Andhra came later at Kakinada in 1923; Madras is outside Andhra.
t: Discriminate the 1921 Bezawada AICC meeting from the 1923 Kakinada session.

x: All four pairs are correct: Satya Doota was the first Telugu journal, Andhra Prakasika the first political journal, Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam (1901) the first Telugu library in Hyderabad and C.P. Brown compiled the English–Telugu dictionary.
t: Check each pair separately.

x: Both are true: Kandukuri Veeresalingam conducted the first widow remarriage in Andhra at Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881, and he also wrote Rajasekhara Charitram, the first Telugu novel.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Vallabhaneni Sitamahalakshmi was the first woman arrested in the Salt Satyagraha in Andhra, and Nyapati Subba Rao was the first Andhra lawyer to boycott British courts.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Kalamalla inscription is the first Telugu inscription, the Magallu inscription first mentions the Kakatiyas, the first Muslim invasion of Warangal came in 1303 and that sultanate attack was sent by Alauddin Khilji, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Discriminate the Kalamalla inscription from the Magallu inscription.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: the 1913 Bapatla Mahasabha is regarded as the first Telugu session, and it demanded a separate Andhra university, but that demand is not why it is called the first session.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: B.N. Sarma (Bayya Narasimheswara Sarma) presided over the first Andhra Mahasabha at Bapatla in 1913. Nyapati Subba Rao led the Andhra Congress Circle and Govinda Rao Nanal the Hyderabad State Congress.
t: Recall the President of the 1913 Bapatla conference.

x: Satya Doota was published from Bellary, the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam was founded in 1901, Komarraju Lakshmana Rao was linked with that Nilayam, and the first Kisan School was at Nidubrolu, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the place or year of each item.

x: Both are true: the first Rayalaseema Mahasabha is linked with Madras on 28 January (dated 1934 or 1936 in different texts), and Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah permitted the English factory at Machilipatnam in 1611.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Option C is incorrect: Anamakonda (Hanamakonda) was only the first Kakatiya capital; the capital later moved to Warangal (Orugallu). Paithan for the Satavahanas, Vengipuram for the Salankayanas and Vijayapuri for the Ikshvakus are right.
t: Watch for the word "only" in a statement.

x: Both are true: Prolaya Vema Reddy ruled from Addanki, Anapota Reddy moved the Reddy capital to Kondaveedu, and after the battle of Tallikota (1565) Vijayanagara shifted its capital to Penugonda.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Satavahanas ruled from Paithan (Pratishthana), the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri, the Salankayanas from Vengipuram and the Musunuri Nayaks from Rekapalli, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the capital of each dynasty.

x: The Kakatiyas first ruled from Anamakonda (Ammakonda) and later moved the capital to Warangal (Orugallu). Koduru was the Brihatpalayana capital, Bodhan the Assaka capital and Vengipuram the Salankayana capital.
t: Recall the later Kakatiya capital.

x: Mahishmathi was the capital of Anupa, one of the regions under Gautamiputra Satakarni. Bodhan was the Assaka capital, Vengipuram the Salankayana capital and Koduru the Brihatpalayana capital under Jayavarma.
t: Link each capital to its kingdom.

x: Bodhan (Potana) was the capital of the Assaka Janapada. Vijayapuri was the Ikshvaku capital, Paithan the Satavahana capital and Koduru the Brihatpalayana capital.
t: Recall the capital of each kingdom.

x: The Kakatiyas first ruled from Anamakonda (Ammakonda), the Assaka Janapada from Bodhan, Anupa from Mahishmathi and the Brihatpalayanas from Koduru, giving a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii.
t: Recall the capital of each kingdom.

x: All three are correct: the Kakatiya capital was first Anamakonda (Ammakonda) and later Warangal (Orugallu), and Bodhan was the capital of the Assaka Janapada.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Koduru was the capital of the Brihatpalayanas, whose known king is Jayavarma, so option B is right. The other options pair dynasties with their own capitals, Vijayapuri, Vengipuram and Paithan, which have nothing to do with Koduru.
t: Link Koduru to its dynasty.

x: The Satavahanas ruled from Paithan, the Ikshvakus from Vijayapuri, the Salankayanas from Vengipuram and the Kakatiyas later from Warangal (Orugallu), giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the capital of each dynasty.

x: Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State in 1953, Penugonda of Vijayanagara after Tallikota, Mahishmathi of Anupa under Gautamiputra Satakarni and Koduru of the Brihatpalayanas under Jayavarma, giving a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the capital of each state.

x: The Reddy kingdom was founded with Addanki as its capital under Prolaya Vema Reddy, and Anapota Reddy later shifted it to Kondaveedu. Anamakonda to Warangal is the Kakatiya sequence.
t: Recall the Reddy capital sequence.

x: Option C is incorrect: Kurnool, not Penugonda, was the capital of Andhra State in 1953; Penugonda was the Vijayanagara capital after Tallikota. The Kakatiya, Assaka and Brihatpalayana capitals are right.
t: Check the capital in each statement.

x: Both are true: after the defeat at Tallikota (1565) Vijayanagara moved its capital to Penugonda, and Anupa, conquered by Gautamiputra Satakarni, had Mahishmathi as its capital.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: the Musunuri capital was Rekapalli, Andhra State's capital in 1953 was Kurnool, and the Assaka Janapada's capital was Bodhan.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: The Kakatiya capital was first Anamakonda and later Warangal (Orugallu), Koduru was the Brihatpalayana capital under Jayavarma, and Bodhan was the Assaka capital, giving a-ii, b-iv, c-iii, d-i.
t: Separate the early and later Kakatiya capitals.

x: Andhra State was formed in 1953 (1 October), with Kurnool as its capital. The other options, Mahishmathi, Penugonda and Kurnool, are capitals, not years.
t: Pick the option that is a year.

x: Hala wrote the Gatha Saptasati, Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Saka ruler Nahapana, Ganapatideva moved the Kakatiya capital to Warangal and Anapota Reddy moved the Reddy capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu, giving a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall each ruler's main achievement.

x: Option C is incorrect: Karpura Vasanta Rayalu was the title of Kumaragiri Reddy, not Pratapa Rudra. Hala as Kavivatsala, Rudramadevi as Rayagaja Kesari and Gautamiputra Satakarni as Thrisamudrapati are right.
t: Link each title to its ruler.

x: Both are true: Recharla Rudra, Ganapatideva's general, built the Ramappa Temple and was called Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya, and Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) built 108 Saiva temples known as Narendreswara temples.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All four are correct: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324, Kumaragiri Reddy wrote Vasantarajeeyam and was a dance expert, Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sangeeta Chintamani and Sahitya Chintamani, and Kapaya Nayaka was called Andhra Suratran.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Rudra Deva became king in 1158, Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Warangal by 1254, Rudramadevi succeeded him in 1260 and Pratapa Rudra came to the throne in 1296, giving A, B, C, D.
t: Arrange the Kakatiya events by year.

x: Gunaga Vijayaditya (Vijayaditya III) of the Eastern Chalukyas bore the title Tripura-Martya-Maheswara. Kollabhighanda was Vijayaditya IV's title, Rayagaja Kesari Rudramadevi's and Sarvagna Pedakomati Vema Reddy's.
t: Link each title to its ruler.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Vijayaditya IV was an Eastern Chalukya king and bore the title Kollabhighanda, but his dynasty is not the reason for that title.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Ganapatideva, the greatest Kakatiya ruler, extended the kingdom south as far as Kanchi. Kondaveedu and Addanki were later Reddy capitals, and Nellore was one of his conquests on the way.
t: Recall the southern limit of Ganapatideva's kingdom.

x: Rudramadevi bore the title Rayagaja Kesari. Karpura Vasanta Rayalu was Kumaragiri Reddy's title, Kollabhighanda Vijayaditya IV's and Andhra Suratran Kapaya Nayaka's.
t: Link each title to its ruler.

x: All three are correct: Prolaya Vema Reddy, founder of the Reddy kingdom, bore the titles Dharma Pratishtana Nagarudu, Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava and Rachur Durgavibhala.
t: Recall the titles of Prolaya Vema Reddy.

x: Pedakomati Vema Reddy bore the title Sarvagna (Sarvagna Chakravarti). Kavisarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, Abhinava Dandi Ketana's and Desha Bhakta Konda Venkatappaiah's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote both Sangeeta Chintamani and Sahitya Chintamani, Kumaragiri Reddy wrote Vasantarajeeyam and Hala wrote Gatha Saptasati. The code pairs items in order when List-II repeats, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall the author of each work.

x: Kapaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family bore the title Andhra Suratran. Kavivatsala was Hala's title, Tripura-Martya-Maheswara Gunaga Vijayaditya's and Kavisarvabhauma Srinatha's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Srinatha, the Reddy-period poet, was known as Kavisarvabhauma. Abhinava Dandi was Ketana's title, Sarvagna Pedakomati Vema Reddy's and Rayagaja Kesari Rudramadevi's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Ketana, a Kakatiya-period poet, bore the title Abhinava Dandi. Desha Bhakta was Konda Venkatappaiah's title, Kollabhighanda Vijayaditya IV's and Andhra Kesari Tanguturi Prakasam's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Tanguturi Prakasam was called Andhra Kesari (Lion of Andhra). Kavisarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, Mlecchabdhi Kumbodbhava Prolaya Vema Reddy's and Desha Bhakta Konda Venkatappaiah's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Konda Venkatappaiah was known as Desha Bhakta. Andhra Suratran was Kapaya Nayaka's title, Sarvagna Pedakomati Vema Reddy's and Andhra Kesari Tanguturi Prakasam's.
t: Link each title to its holder.

x: Vijayaditya II (Narendra Mrigaraja) of the Eastern Chalukyas built 108 Saiva temples called Narendreswara temples. Vijayaditya IV was Kollabhighanda, Gunaga Vijayaditya was Vijayaditya III, and Rudra Deva was a Kakatiya.
t: Discriminate among the Vijayadityas.

x: Both are true: Hala, author of Gatha Saptasati, and Gautamiputra Satakarni, conqueror of Nahapana, were both Satavahana kings.
t: Recall the dynasty of each king.

x: All four are correct: Gunaga Vijayaditya, also written Gunga Vijayaditya (Vijayaditya III), won victories over Nellore, Kiranapura and Achalapura.
t: Recall the victories of Gunaga Vijayaditya.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Rudra Deva, a Kakatiya ruler, built the Thousand-Pillar Temple at Hanamakonda (1163), but his dynasty is not the reason he built it.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: I and II are correct: Ganapatideva and Rudramadevi were Kakatiya rulers. III is false because Recharla Rudra was a Kakatiya general from the Recherla family, not a member of the dynasty.
t: Discriminate rulers of a dynasty from their generals.

x: All four were Reddy rulers: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the kingdom, Anapota Reddy moved the capital to Kondaveedu, and Kumaragiri Reddy and Pedakomati Vema Reddy were later kings.
t: Recall the Reddy kings.

x: Both are true: Kapaya Nayaka belonged to the Musunuri family, and Srinatha was a court poet of the Reddy period under Pedakomati Vema Reddy.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true: Ketana, author of Dasakumara Charitra, was a Kakatiya-period poet, and Tanguturi Prakasam was a modern freedom fighter and the first CM of Andhra State.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Konda Venkatappaiah, called Desha Bhakta, was a modern freedom fighter of the Andhra Movement. The Reddy, Kakatiya and Satavahana periods are medieval and ancient.
t: Place the person in the right period.

x: Devinaganika (Naganika), the Satavahana queen, is the intended answer: she ruled as regent for her minor sons after Satakarni I died. The item is doubtful because it names her son "Mallamma"; Mallamma Devi was actually a queen of Bobbili.
t: Recall the Satavahana queen who acted as regent.

x: Option A is incorrect: Mallamma Devi was the queen of Bobbili in the 1757 Bobbili–Vizianagaram battle; Pedakomati Vema Reddy's queen was Surambika. The other three statements are right.
t: Check the ruler named in each statement.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Rudramadevi succeeded her father Ganapatideva, and she took the throne in 1260, but the year does not explain why she succeeded.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana, Ganapatideva moved the capital to Warangal in 1254, Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324 and Hala bore the title Kavivatsala, giving a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i.
t: Recall each ruler's main achievement.

x: Both are true: the Ikshvaku king Virapurushadatta's reign was the golden age of Buddhism, and Surambika, queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy, dug the Santana Sagaram tank.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Mallamma Devi was the queen of Bobbili during the Bobbili–Vizianagaram battle of 1757. Surambika was a Reddy queen, Devinaganika a Satavahana queen and Rudramadevi a Kakatiya ruler.
t: Link each queen to her kingdom.

x: Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in dance and wrote Vasantarajeeyam on it. Pedakomati Vema Reddy wrote Sangeeta Chintamani, Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the kingdom, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.
t: Recall the Reddy ruler linked with dance.

x: Rudramadevi was a Kakatiya, Hala a Satavahana, Virapurushadatta an Ikshvaku and Prolaya Vema Reddy a Reddy ruler, giving a-ii, b-i, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the dynasty of each ruler.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Gautamiputra Satakarni was a Satavahana, and the Kakatiya Ganapatideva moved his capital to Warangal in 1254; the two facts are about different dynasties.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Devinaganika (Naganika), wife of Satakarni I and regent for her minor sons, belonged to the Satavahana dynasty. Rudramadevi was Kakatiya and Surambika a Reddy queen.
t: Recall the dynasty of each queen.

x: Surambika was the queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy and dug the Santana Sagaram tank. Kumaragiri and Prolaya Vema were other Reddy kings, and Ganapatideva was a Kakatiya.
t: Link each queen to her king.

x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated the Saka (Kshaharata) ruler Nahapana, as the Nasik inscription records. Hala was a poet-king, Virapurushadatta an Ikshvaku and Ganapatideva a Kakatiya.
t: Recall the Satavahana who defeated Nahapana.

x: Both are true: Virapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king of Vijayapuri, and Hala, author of Gatha Saptasati, was a Satavahana king.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Hala was a Satavahana king and was called Kavivatsala, but the title comes from his love of poetry, not from his dynasty.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: All three are correct: Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom, Kumaragiri Reddy was an expert in dance, and Surambika dug the Santana Sagaram tank.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Devinaganika was a Satavahana queen, Surambika dug the Santana Sagaram tank, Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and Kumaragiri Reddy was a dance expert, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.
t: Recall what each person is known for.

x: Three are Satavahana: Devinaganika, Hala and Gautamiputra Satakarni. Virapurushadatta was an Ikshvaku king.
t: Recall the dynasty of each person.

x: Ganapatideva shifted the capital to Warangal in 1254, Rudramadevi took the throne in 1260, Prolaya Vema Reddy founded the Reddy kingdom in 1324 and the Bobbili–Vizianagaram battle took place in 1757, giving B, C, A, D.
t: Arrange the events by year.

x: The Bobbili–Vizianagaram battle was fought in 1757, when Bussy and the Vizianagaram ruler attacked Bobbili fort. 1254, 1260 and 1324 are Kakatiya and Reddy dates.
t: Recall the year of the battle.

x: Surambika, queen of Pedakomati Vema Reddy, dug the Santana Sagaram tank. The other names are made-up distractors.
t: Recall the tank linked with Surambika.

x: N.T. Rama Rao founded the Telugu Desam Party on 29 May 1982 and won power in 1983. Nadendla Bhaskara Rao later formed the Democratic Telugu Desam, and Chenna Reddy led the Telangana Praja Samithi.
t: Recall the founder of each party.

x: Option C is incorrect: the Democratic Telugu Desam Party was formed by Nadendla Bhaskara Rao, not N.T. Rama Rao, who founded the Telugu Desam Party. The other statements are right.
t: Discriminate the Telugu Desam from the Democratic Telugu Desam.

x: Both are true and R explains A: Virapurushadatta's reign is called the golden age of Buddhism because Buddhism flourished at Nagarjunakonda under him.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: This item is doubtful: Marco Polo visited Andhra under Rudramadevi and Nicolo Conti visited Vijayanagara under Devaraya I, but Nuniz came under Achyutadeva Raya, so pair d (Devaraya I reigning during Nuniz's visit) is false. Option D is keyed only by default.
t: Link each traveller to the ruler of his time.

x: Both are true: under Ganapatideva the Kakatiya capital moved from Hanamakonda to Warangal, and Rajamahendra (Rajahmundry) was built by the Eastern Chalukyas.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: N.G. Ranga was the first President of the Andhra Socialist Party, Nadendla Bhaskara Rao formed the Democratic Telugu Desam, Marri Chenna Reddy led the Telangana Praja Samithi and the Communist Party started the Visalandhra Movement, giving a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Link each leader or party to its role.

x: Both are true: the Nasik inscription was set up by Gautami Balasri, mother of Gautamiputra Satakarni, in the 19th year of her grandson Vasishtiputra Pulomavi.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Rudramadevi, the Kakatiya queen whose kingdom Marco Polo visited, was also called Rudramba. Gautami Balasri was a Satavahana queen mother and Bodhisri an Ikshvaku-period Buddhist lay devotee.
t: Recall the other name of Rudramadevi.

x: Both are true: Upasika Bodhisri built a chaitya at Nagarjunakonda in the Ikshvaku period, and Rajamahendra (Rajahmundry) was built by the Eastern Chalukyas.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: All three are correct: the Kakatiya capital moved from Hanamakonda to Warangal under Ganapatideva, Rajamahendra is today's Rajahmundry, and Nuniz visited Vijayanagara under Achyutadeva Raya.
t: Check each statement separately.

x: Option C is incorrect: Nicolo Conti (c. 1420) was the earliest European visitor to Vijayanagara; Harihara-I was its first ruler. The statements on Prakrit inscriptions, the Satavahanas and Megasthenes are right.
t: Discriminate rulers from foreign visitors.

x: Both are true but R does not explain A: Kundakundacharya is linked with the Jain Syadvada school, which is also called the seven-fold predication (Sapta-bhangi-naya), but his link does not explain that name.
t: Check whether R is the cause of A.

x: Rudramadevi succeeded Ganapatideva, Saluva Narasimha ruled before Krishnadevaraya, Mahadeva followed Rudra Deva and Kumaragiri Reddy followed Anavema Reddy, giving a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii. Strictly, Krishnadevaraya's immediate predecessor was Vira Narasimha Raya, so pair b is loose.
t: Recall the order of succession in each dynasty.

x: All four are correct: Salar Jung brought in the Zilla-bandi system in 1865, the Collector's office came to the North Sarkars under Cornwallis's system, Mahboob Ali Khan issued the Mulki rules in 1888, and B.N. Sarma moved the linguistic provinces resolution in 1918.
t: Check the person and year in each statement.

x: This item is doubtful: Rudramba and Rudramadevi are the same Kakatiya queen, who succeeded Ganapatideva in 1260, so options A and C both fit. Option A is keyed; Pratapa Rudra came in 1296 and Kumaragiri Reddy was a Reddy king.
t: Watch for two names of the same person.

x: The French general Bussy is remembered for his success in Deccan affairs, controlling the Nizam's court and gaining the Northern Circars for the French. Salar Jung began Zilla-bandi, Cornwallis the Collector's office and the Nizam the Mulki rules.
